description: Hysteresis-Buffered Consensus Phase Selection: Step 1: Maintain two independent phase-saving arrays, `phase_focused[v]` and `phase_stable[v]`. During backtracking, update only the array corresponding to the solver's current search mode (focused/exploration vs. stable/exploitation). Step 2: Maintain a phase quality matrix `phase_score[v][2]` (tracking scores for True and False assignments). During conflict analysis, for each variable involved in the conflict, add `1.0 / LBD` to `phase_score[v][assigned_phase]`. Decay all scores by a factor of 0.95 at every restart. Step 3: Inside `kissat_decide_phase(v)`, identify the current search mode and retrieve the baseline candidate phase: `P = phase_focused[v]` if in focused mode, otherwise `P = phase_stable[v]`. Step 4: Evaluate the historical LBD quality of the candidate phase. If the opposite phase has a significantly better track record—specifically, if `phase_score[v][!P] > 1.5 * phase_score[v][P]` AND `phase_score[v][!P] > 2.0` (minimum confidence threshold)—override the baseline and select `!P`. Step 5: If the override conditions in Step 4 are not met, evaluate the consensus between the two modes. If `phase_focused[v] == phase_stable[v]`, return the consensus phase `P`. If the modes disagree (i.e., `phase_focused[v] != phase_stable[v]`), apply a hysteresis buffer: if the score of the non-baseline phase is at least 10% higher than the baseline phase (`phase_score[v][!P] > 1.1 * phase_score[v][P]`), select `!P`. Otherwise, default to the baseline candidate phase `P` to preserve mode-specific search continuity.
parent_algorithm_description: Cross-Mode Consensus Phase Selection: Step 1: Maintain two independent phase-saving arrays, `phase_focused[v]` and `phase_stable[v]`. During backtracking, update only the array corresponding to the solver's current search mode (focused/exploration vs. stable/exploitation). Step 2: Maintain a phase quality matrix `phase_score[v][2]` (tracking scores for True and False assignments). During conflict analysis, for each variable involved in the conflict, add `1.0 / LBD` to `phase_score[v][assigned_phase]`. Decay all scores by a factor of 0.95 at every restart. Step 3: Inside `kissat_decide_phase(v)`, identify the current search mode and retrieve the baseline candidate phase: `P = phase_focused[v]` if in focused mode, otherwise `P = phase_stable[v]`. Step 4: Evaluate the historical LBD quality of the candidate phase. If the opposite phase has a significantly better track record—specifically, if `phase_score[v][!P] > 1.5 * phase_score[v][P]` AND `phase_score[v][!P] > 2.0` (minimum confidence threshold)—override the baseline and select `!P`. Step 5: If the override conditions in Step 4 are not met, evaluate the consensus between the two modes. If `phase_focused[v] == phase_stable[v]`, return the consensus phase `P`. If the modes disagree (i.e., `phase_focused[v] != phase_stable[v]`), return the phase that has the strictly higher `phase_score[v]`, breaking any exact ties by returning the baseline candidate phase `P`.
analysis: In Step 5 of the original algorithm, when the focused and stable modes disagreed, the solver blindly selected the phase with the strictly higher score. Because scores decay and update frequently, a microscopic difference (e.g., 0.001) could cause the solver to flip its phase choice, leading to phase thrashing and disrupting the current search mode's trajectory. By introducing a 10% hysteresis buffer in this variant's Step 5, the solver only abandons its mode-specific baseline phase when the alternative phase is demonstrably better. This preserves the distinct exploratory/exploitative behaviors of Kissat's modes while still resolving significant disagreements intelligently, ultimately reducing search tree churn and improving PAR2 times.
